ground_truth: The new `Subquery.resolve_expression()` is meant to drop the Subquery shim and return the bare resolved `Query`. It is supposed to wrap the query in an `ExpressionWrapper` only when the user passed an `output_field` that differs from the query's own. It tests this with `self.output_field != resolved.query.output_field`, but `Field.__eq__` compares fields by `creation_counter` and model, not by kind. So a separately instantiated field such as `IntegerField()` never equals the query's model field. As a result, any `Subquery(..., output_field=X())` is always wrapped in an `ExpressionWrapper`, even when `X` is the same field type as the selected column. Lookups that introspect the right-hand side as a `Query` then no longer recognize it, defeating the purpose of the change. One example is the tuple lookups' `isinstance(self.rhs, Query)` check, which is supposed to raise `NotSupportedError` for composite-pk comparisons against subqueries. The fix compares field types (`type(self.output_field) is not type(resolved.query.output_field)`) instead of using field equality.
